city_fields.supportSceneAlt: A doula walking alongside a pregnant mom along a palm-lined Hialeah street: South Florida birth support and doula care
city_fields.culture: Hialeah sits at the western edge of the Miami metro, a city of about 240,000 people where Spanish is the language of the neighborhood as much as English. It sits right between downtown Miami and the airport corridor, and it has grown into one of South Florida's densest pockets of birthing-related services: a hospital with its own Maternity Child Care Center, a freestanding birth center in North Miami Beach about fifteen minutes away, and a doula market that runs from independent Hialeah practices to multi-practice agencies. Most Hialeah births still happen at Palmetto General Hospital or at the Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital a few minutes west, and the midwife community is growing around those two anchors.
city_fields.medicaidNote: Yes - Florida Medicaid (Family Choice managed care plans for Miami-Dade) has covered doula services for eligible families since 2023 under the state's doula coverage rule. Check your specific Family Choice plan about which doulas are in-network, or ask an enrolled doula directly; several Hialeah-area practices already work with Medicaid families.
